validated_results.title: Both high and low levels of blood vitamin D are associated with a higher prostate cancer risk: a longitudinal, nested case-control study in the Nordic countries.
validated_results.reason: Longitudinal nested case-control study of serum 25(OH)-vitamin D concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk in Nordic men, providing a population-wide exposure-outcome relationship.

extraction.comparison_type: Low (</=19 nmol/l) and high (>/=80 nmol/l) serum 25(OH)-vitamin D versus normal average concentration (40-60 nmol/l)
extraction.timing: prospective (longitudinal nested case-control using prediagnostic stored serum)
extraction.population: Nordic men with banked serum samples

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a longitudinal nested case-control study on Nordic men (Norway, Finland and Sweden) using serum banks of 200,000 samples. We studied serum 25(OH)-vitamin D levels of 622 prostate cancer cases and 1,451 matched controls and found that both low (</=19 nmol/l) and high (>/=80 nmol/l) 25(OH)-vitamin D serum concentrations are associated with higher prostate cancer risk.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods/results sentence; total_n derived from reported group counts 622 + 1451 = 2073

cases.excerpt: We studied serum 25(OH)-vitamin D levels of 622 prostate cancer cases and 1,451 matched controls and found that both low (</=19 nmol/l) and high (>/=80 nmol/l) 25(OH)-vitamin D serum concentrations are associated with higher prostate cancer risk.

validated_results.title: Protective effect of green tea against prostate cancer: a case-control study in southeast China.
validated_results.reason: Case-control study of green tea consumption with adjusted odds ratios for incident histologically confirmed prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Tea drinkers (almost all green tea) versus non-tea drinkers
extraction.timing: retrospective (interview-assessed usual tea consumption in incident cases and controls, 2001-2002)
extraction.population: 130 incident patients with histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma and 274 age-matched hospital inpatient controls

sample_size.excerpt: The cases were 130 incident patients with histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The controls were 274 hospital inpatients without prostate cancer or any other malignant diseases, and matched to the age of cases.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods sentences; total_n derived from reported group counts 130 + 274 = 404

cases.excerpt: The cases were 130 incident patients with histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate.

effect_size.excerpt: The prostate cancer risk declined with increasing frequency, duration and quantity of green tea consumption. The adjusted odds ratio (OR), relative to non-tea drinkers, were 0.28 (95% CI = 0.17-0.47) for tea drinking, 0.12 (95% CI = 0.06-0.26) for drinking tea over 40 years, 0.09 (95% CI = 0.04-0.21) for those consuming more than 1.5 kg of tea leaves yearly, and 0.27 (95% CI = 0.15-0.48) for those drinking more than 3 cups (1 litre) daily.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The adjusted odds ratio (OR), relative to non-tea drinkers, were 0.28 (95% CI = 0.17-0.47) for tea drinking, 0.12 (95% CI = 0.06-0.26) for drinking tea over 40 years, 0.09 (95% CI = 0.04-0.21) for those consuming more than 1.5 kg of tea leaves yearly, and 0.27 (95% CI = 0.15-0.48) for those drinking more than 3 cups (1 litre) daily.

design.excerpt: a case-control study was conducted in Hangzhou, southeast China during 2001-2002
